p1: The king made a man named Haman his most important leader. Everyone had to bow low to Haman to show him honor.
But Mordecai would not bow. Haman was full of anger and pride. He thought he was better than everyone else.
Haman knew Mordecai was a Jew. So he made a mean plan to hurt all of Mordecai’s people.
p2: Haman told the king, “These people do not keep your laws.” So the king gave Haman his ring, which stamped the king’s rules.
Don’t worry, this story has a happy ending! Haman chose pride, but Jesus teaches us to be kind. Tonight, think of one kind thing to do tomorrow.
old: There was a very proud man named Haman who worked for the king. Haman wanted everyone to bow down low to him whenever he walked by.
Everybody bowed — everybody except Mordecai. Mordecai was kind and respectful, but he only bowed down to worship Heavenly Father.
This made proud Haman very angry. But Mordecai stood quietly and firmly. He knew that worship belongs only to Heavenly Father.
Mordecai was not being unkind — he was being faithful. It can take courage to do what’s right when everyone else is doing something different. Heavenly Father is pleased when we stand tall for Him.
